text: Then, on the night before she left, while she was packing up in her grandmothers house on Nuns Island, she suddenly heard gravel thrown up against the window of her room. <break time="0.8s" /> The window was so wet with rain that she could not see out, so she ran downstairs as she was and slipped out the back into the garden, where the poor boy stood shivering at the end. <break time="0.8s" /> She begged him to go home at once, warning him that he would get his death in the rain, but he only said that he did not want to live. <break time="0.8s" /> Even now, she cried, she could see his eyes as well as well, and she remembered how he had stood at the end of the wall, where there was a tree, in the rain. <break time="0.8s" /> Scarcely had she spent a week at the convent in Dublin when news came that Michael Furey had died and had been buried in Oughterard, where his people came from. <break time="0.8s" /> Choking with sobs, she broke off and, overcome by emotion, flung herself face downward on the bed, while Gabriel held her hand a moment longer, uncertain what he should do. <break time="0.8s" /> Then, shy of intruding on her grief, he let her hand fall gently and walked quietly to the window, and by the time he turned to look at her again, she was fast asleep.
